newsitem.title: USA: Benefits of last minute shopping.
newsitem.headline: Benefits of last minute shopping.

text.p: Calling all last minute holiday shoppers. You may not be as bad off as you think. Hitting the stores at the 11th hour may actually pay off, an informal survey from Babson College shows.

"Holding off until only a day or two before Christmas for buying gifts is more efficient fincancially and psychologically," said Dr. Kathleen Seiders, a marketing professor and consumer behaviour expert at the Wellesley, Mass., college.
Last minute shoppers are more likely than their more timely counterparts to spend less because they are focused on one task, such as a sweater for Grandma or snow jackets for the twins.
"Shoppers shop for themselves as well as others. But last minute shoppers are likely to spend more on others" than for themselves, Seiders said.
Those who cut it close benefit from last-minute markdowns and get the best prices, she said.
They can put off credit-card statements until the next year (which is actually only a week after Chirstmas) and get more time on 30-day return policies.
Because they are shopping late in the month, last minute shoppers are more likely to have received any Christmas bonuses, taking some of the strain off their cash flow, she added.

On a psychological level, being a last minute shopper allows more time before entering stores to research the latest trends in clothes or toys. It also allows time to check what the gift getter really wants or has already received.
For those who hate shopping, the last minute dash keeps the agony short-lived. And, if time is precious, stores are open late right before Christmas.
Last minute shopping is not for everyone, Seiders said, and requires flexibility.

One key to this type of shopping is to have three or four gift ideas per person. "You can't set your heart on any one thing. You have to compromise," because the items may be sold out by the time you arrive for your shopping expedition, Seiders said.

"This year (late shopping) might be even more of a challenge because (store) inventories are low," she said. But, "an opportunistic shopper can really have a great time," seeking out bargains, unusual gifts and some odds and ends.
Men are more likely than women to be last minute shoppers, at a male-female ratio of about 60/40 to 70/30, she said. This is the reverse of the norm, with 70 percent of all shoppers female.
Are you a last minute shopper? Seiders says you fit the profile if you:
-- Are organisationally challenged -- clueless about what to buy, where to go and when to do it.
-- Are a thrill seeker who thrives on chaos.
-- Are a holiday-hater who deals with the season only because you have to.
-- Are indecisive and get anxious about deciding on gifts.
-- Are deadline driven and only act in emergencies.
-- Are a bargain hunter who sniffs out every opportunity to find a deal.

If you want to put a little something special in a loved one's Christmas stocking, why not give the best for your money? Travel & Leisure magazine has cited the world's best hotels for value -- those offering travelers the most for magic for the money.

Travel & Leisure, in its January issue, asked a group of frequent and experienced travelers to vote for the best travel values in various categories. The winners are not necessarily the most expensive, because the goal is to get the best value for your money.
Australia scored high in the survey, offering winners in value for several hotels and the Great Barrier Reef resort area.

The overall winner as best hotel in the world for value was the Marriott Casa Magna, Cancun, Mexico. Modelled after an imperial Roman villa, the Casa Magna "brings a splash of Vegas to the sun and fun of Cancun," the magazine says. It also won in the moderate ($250 per night and less) category.
Sidney, Australia, won as the world's best city for value. It was cited for not only its good values, but its friendly people as well, Travel & Leisure said.
The world's best island/resort area for value is Australia's Great Barrier Reef.
Hawaii was well represented in the top 10 island/resorts, because even though Hawaii is part of the United States, it feels like a foreign destination.

In the deluxe ($350 a night or more) category, the world's best hotel for value is the MalaMala Game Reserve, South Africa. This "camp" is set on South Africa's largest private game reserve, affording views of lions, elephants, leopards, rhinoceros and buffalo. The lodge accepts only 50 guests at a time and has a staff-to-guest ratio of three-to-one.

In the moderate ($250-$350 a night) category, Melbourne, Australia's Sofitel won. Overlooking the city, each room has a view of the bay, the skyline and the public gardens around the city centre. Since many guests are business travelers, each room has a desk and a separate line for fax or modem.
